name: Hand
overview: The Scriptures reveal the hand as a powerful symbol of authority, consecration, and divine interaction. In the sacrificial system, Aaron and his sons laid their hands on offerings to signify atonement and dedication, as seen in the bullock and rams of Exodus 29 and the burnt offering in Leviticus 1. The hand also conveys blessing and honor, illustrated by Israel's deliberate placement of his right and left hands on Ephraim and Manasseh in Genesis 48, and Abram's lifted hand as a solemn pledge to God in Genesis 14. These examples collectively emphasize the hand's role in God's covenantal relationship with His people, marking acts of dedication, blessing, and solemn oath.
